title.zh: 卷307 列傳九十四 尹继善 刘于义 陈大受 张允随 陈宏谋
title.en: Volume 307 Biographies 94: Yin Jishan, Liu Yuyi, Chen Dashou, Zhang Yunsui, Chen Hongmou
title.raw: 卷307 列傳九十四 尹继善 刘于义 陈大受 张允随 陈宏谋

sentences.zh: 尹繼善劉於義陳大受張允隨陳宏謀

translations.literal: Yin Jishan, Liu Yuyi, Chen Dashou, Zhang Yunsui, Chen Hongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan, Liu Yuyi, Chen Dashou, Zhang Yunsui, and Chen Hongmou.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善，字元長，章佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，大學士尹泰子。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan, courtesy name Yuanchang, of the Zhangjia clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was the son of Grand Secretary Yin Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan, styled Yuanchang, belonged to the Zhangjia clan and served as a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner; he was the son of Grand Secretary Yin Tai.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he passed the jinshi examination, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the first year of Yongzheng, entered the Hanlin as a probationary academician, and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷侍講，尋署戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to lecturer, and soon after served as acting director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he rose to Hanlin lecturer and shortly thereafter acted as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上遣通政使留保等如廣東按布政使官達、按察使方原瑛受賕狀，以尹繼善偕。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Communications Commissioner Liubao and others to Guangdong to investigate charges of bribery against Provincial Administration Commissioner Guanda and Surveillance Commissioner Fang Yuanying, with Yin Jishan accompanying them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched Communications Commissioner Liubao and others to Guangdong to look into bribery charges against Administration Commissioner Guanda and Surveillance Commissioner Fang Yuanying, and Yin Jishan went with them.

sentences.zh: 鞫實，即以尹繼善署按察使。

translations.literal: When the investigation proved the charges true, Yin Jishan was at once made acting surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Once the inquiry confirmed the offenses, Yin Jishan was immediately appointed acting surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，授內閣侍讀學士，協理江南河務。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed reader in the Grand Secretariat and was assigned to assist in managing Jiangnan river works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became a Grand Secretariat reader and was put in charge of assisting with Jiangnan hydraulic affairs.

sentences.zh: 是秋，署江蘇巡撫，七年，真除。

translations.literal: That autumn he served as acting governor of Jiangsu; in the seventh year he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he acted as Jiangsu governor, and in the seventh year the post was confirmed to him.

sentences.zh: 疏禁收漕規費，定石米費六分，半給旗丁，半給州縣，使無不足，然後裁以法。

translations.literal: He memorialized to forbid collection of irregular grain-transport fees, fixing the per-shi rice charge at six fen, half for banner transport troops and half for prefectures and counties so that none would be short, and only then to reduce it by statute.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial banning illicit surcharges on grain transport, setting a levy of six fen per shi of rice—half for banner transport crews and half for local prefectures and counties so that all parties were adequately provided for before any statutory reduction was applied.

sentences.zh: 平糶盈餘，非公家之利，應存縣庫，常平倉捐穀聽民樂輸，不得隨漕勒徵。

translations.literal: Surpluses from relief grain sales were not public profit and should be kept in county treasuries; grain donated to ever-normal granaries should be accepted only as the people wished to give, and must not be forcibly levied along with transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: He held that surpluses from government grain sales at relief prices were not state revenue and should remain in county treasuries, that donations to ever-normal granaries should be voluntary, and that such gifts must not be extorted along with transport dues.

sentences.zh: 命如議行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that his proposals be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 又疏請崇明增設巡道，兼轄太倉、通州。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to add an inspection circuit at Chongming with concurrent jurisdiction over Taicang and Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that a new inspection circuit be established at Chongming with authority over Taicang and Tongzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 並釐定永興、牛羊、大安諸沙分防將吏。

translations.literal: He also fixed the officers assigned to garrison the sandbanks at Yongxing, Niuyang, and Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise reorganized the officers responsible for defending the Yongxing, Niuyang, and Da'an sandbanks.

sentences.zh: 福山增隸沙船，與京口、狼山諸汛會哨。

translations.literal: Fushan was added to the jurisdiction of sand-junk patrols, which were to join in joint patrols with the garrisons at Jingkou, Langshan, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Fushan was brought under the sand-junk patrol system and ordered to conduct joint patrols with the garrisons at Jingkou, Langshan, and other stations.

sentences.zh: 又請移按察使駐蘇州，蘇松道駐上海。

translations.literal: He also asked that the surveillance commissioner be stationed at Suzhou and the Susong circuit intendant at Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed moving the surveillance commissioner to Suzhou and the Susong circuit intendant to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted all of these requests.

sentences.zh: 旋署河道總督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he served as acting director-general of waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He soon afterward acted as director-general of waterways.

sentences.zh: 九年，署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he acted as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 十年，協辦江寧將軍，兼理兩淮鹽政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he assisted in the duties of the Jiangning general and concurrently managed the Lianghuai salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he assisted the Jiangning general and at the same time took charge of the Lianghuai salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「鎮江水兵駐高資港，江寧水兵駐省會，各增置將吏。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Zhenjiang naval troops should be stationed at Gaozi Harbor and the Jiangning naval troops at the provincial capital, with additional officers appointed to each.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Zhenjiang's naval force should be posted at Gaozi Harbor and Jiangning's at the provincial seat, and additional commanders should be assigned to each detachment.

sentences.zh: 狼山復設趕纟曾大船，與鎮江、江寧水兵每月出巡察，庶長江數千里聲勢聯絡。」

translations.literal: At Langshan large fast patrol vessels should again be deployed; together with the Zhenjiang and Jiangning naval forces they should go out on monthly patrols, so that the Yangzi's thousands of li may be linked in a continuous show of force."
translations.idiomatic: Large fast patrol ships should be restored at Langshan and, together with the Zhenjiang and Jiangning fleets, sent out on monthly patrols so that the Yangzi's thousand-mile reach would be covered by a connected chain of naval strength."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the plan.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善請清察江蘇積欠田賦，上遣侍郎彭維新等助為料理，又命浙江總督李衛與其事。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan requested a thorough audit of Jiangsu's accumulated arrears in land tax; the emperor sent Vice Minister Peng Weixin and others to assist in settling the matter, and also ordered Zhejiang Governor-General Li Wei to take part.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan asked for a full investigation of Jiangsu's long-standing land-tax arrears; the throne sent Vice Minister Peng Weixin and others to help settle the accounts and directed Zhejiang Governor-General Li Wei to join the effort.

sentences.zh: 察出康熙五十一年至雍正四年都計積虧一千十一萬，上命分別吏蝕、民欠，逐年帶徵。

translations.literal: The audit found a total accumulated shortfall from the fifty-first year of Kangxi through the fourth year of Yongzheng of 10,110,000 taels; the emperor ordered that embezzlement by officials and arrears owed by the people be distinguished and collected year by year.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation revealed a cumulative deficit of 10.11 million taels from Kangxi 51 through Yongzheng 4; the emperor ordered official embezzlement to be separated from genuine peasant arrears and recovery to proceed on an annual schedule.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善等並議敘。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan and the others were all granted commendatory promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan and his colleagues were all rewarded with merit citations.

sentences.zh: 又請改三江營同知為鹽務道，並增設緝私將吏。

translations.literal: He also asked that the Sanjiang garrison subprefect be changed to a salt commissioner and that additional officers be appointed to suppress smuggling.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed converting the Sanjiang garrison subprefect into a salt intendant and adding officers devoted to anti-smuggling duty.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調雲貴廣西總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be governor-general of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to the post of governor-general of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 思茅土酋刁興國為亂，總督高其倬發兵討之，擒興國，餘黨未解。

translations.literal: The Simao tribal chief Diao Xingguo rose in rebellion; Governor-General Gao Qizhuo sent troops to suppress him, captured Xingguo, but the remaining followers were not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Simao chieftain Diao Xingguo rebelled; Governor-General Gao Qizhuo marched against him and took Xingguo prisoner, yet his followers had not yet been subdued.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善至，諮於其倬，得翾要，檄總兵楊國華、董芳督兵深入，斬其酋三，及從亂者百餘。

translations.literal: When Yin Jishan arrived he consulted Gao Qizhuo and obtained the essentials of the situation, then issued orders to Regional Commanders Yang Guohua and Dong Fang to lead troops deep into the territory, where they beheaded three chiefs and more than a hundred who had joined the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the province Yin Jishan consulted Gao Qizhuo and learned the essentials of the campaign, then ordered Regional Commanders Yang Guohua and Dong Fang to drive deep into rebel country, where they killed three chieftains and more than a hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 元江、臨安悉定。

translations.literal: Yuanjiang and Lin'an were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjiang and Lin'an were fully brought under control.

sentences.zh: 分兵進攻攸樂、思茅，東道撫定攸樂三十六寨，西道攻六囤，破十五寨，降八十餘寨。

translations.literal: Troops were divided to attack Youle and Simao; the eastern route pacified thirty-six stockades in Youle, while the western route attacked Liutun, stormed fifteen stockades, and received the surrender of more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Forces were split to advance on Youle and Simao: the eastern column pacified thirty-six Youle stockades, while the western column assaulted Liutun, took fifteen stockades by storm, and accepted the surrender of more than eighty others.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上諭曰：「剿撫名雖二事，恩威用豈兩端？

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor instructed: "Suppression and pacification are called two policies, but can favor and awe be applied in two different ways?
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the emperor instructed: "Punitive campaigns and conciliatory measures may go by different names, but can kindness and severity really be wielded as two separate tools?

sentences.zh: 當撫者不妨明示優容，當剿者亦宜顯施斬馘，俾知順則利，逆則害。

translations.literal: Where pacification is appropriate, leniency may openly be shown; where suppression is needed, executions should also be displayed, so that they know obedience brings benefit and defiance brings harm.
translations.idiomatic: Where conciliation is called for, show clemency openly; where force is required, make executions visible, so that people learn that submission brings reward and resistance brings ruin.

sentences.zh: 今此攻心之師，即寓將來善後之舉，是乃仁術也。

translations.literal: This campaign that strikes at the heart is itself the means of future good order; this is truly a benevolent method.
translations.idiomatic: This present campaign aimed at winning hearts already contains the work of future pacification; that is the truly humane approach.

sentences.zh: 識之！」

translations.literal: Take heed of this!"
translations.idiomatic: Bear this in mind!"

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏定新闢苗疆諸事，請移清江鎮總兵於台拱，並移設同知以下官，增兵設汛，從之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized to settle affairs in the newly opened Miao frontier, asking that the Qingjiang garrison regional commander be moved to Taigong and that subprefects and lower officials be reassigned, with additional troops and garrisons established; all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he submitted regulations for the newly opened Miao territories, proposing to move the Qingjiang regional commander to Taigong, reassign subprefects and lower officials, and add troops and garrison posts; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏雲南濬土黃河，自土黃至百色，袤七百四十餘裡。

translations.literal: He also reported dredging the Tuhuang River in Yunnan from Tuhuang to Baise, a stretch of more than 740 li.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported dredging Yunnan's Tuhuang River from Tuhuang to Baise, a distance of more than seven hundred forty li.

sentences.zh: 得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: He received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 尋詔廣西仍隸廣東總督。

translations.literal: Soon an edict restored Guangxi to the jurisdiction of the Guangdong governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict placed Guangxi once again under the Guangdong governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十三年，奏定貴州安籠等營製。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized to fix the regulations of the Anlong and other garrisons in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he submitted regulations governing the Anlong garrison and other Guizhou military posts.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗复亂，尹繼善發雲南兵，並徵湖廣、廣西兵策應。

translations.literal: The Miao in Guizhou rebelled again; Yin Jishan dispatched Yunnan troops and also called up forces from Huguang and Guangxi in support.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guizhou Miao rose again, Yin Jishan sent Yunnan troops and summoned reinforcements from Huguang and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 遣副將紀龍剿清平，參將哈尚德收新舊黃平二城，合兵徇重安。

translations.literal: He sent Vice Commander Ji Long to suppress Qingping, Colonel Ha Shangde to recover the old and new Huangping cities, and the combined forces advanced on Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Vice Commander Ji Long against Qingping, Colonel Ha Shangde to retake the old and new Huangping towns, and then united the columns for an advance on Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 副將周儀等復餘慶，獲苗酋羅萬像等。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Zhou Yi and others recovered Yuqing and captured the Miao chiefs Luo Wanxiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Zhou Yi and his colleagues retook Yuqing and captured the Miao chieftains Luo Wanxiang and others.

sentences.zh: 總兵王無黨、韓勳剿八寨，總兵譚行義剿鎮遠。

translations.literal: Regional Commanders Wang Wudang and Han Xun suppressed the Eight Stockades, and Regional Commander Tan Xingyi suppressed Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commanders Wang Wudang and Han Xun campaigned in the Eight Stockades, while Regional Commander Tan Xingyi operated against Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 又令無黨合廣西、湖南兵與行義會，破苗寨，斬千餘級，獲苗酋阿九清等，苗亂乃定。

translations.literal: He also ordered Wudang to join Guangxi and Hunan troops with Xingyi, stormed Miao stockades, killed more than a thousand, and captured the Miao chiefs A Jiuqing and others; the Miao rebellion was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered Wudang to unite Guangxi and Hunan forces with Xingyi's column, stormed Miao stockades, killed more than a thousand rebels, and captured chieftains including A Jiuqing, after which the Miao uprising was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，貴州別設總督，命尹繼善專督雲南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong a separate governor-general was established for Guizhou, and Yin Jishan was ordered to supervise Yunnan alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong Guizhou received its own governor-general, and Yin Jishan was left in sole charge of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 二年，奏豁雲南軍丁銀萬二千二百有奇。

translations.literal: In the second year he memorialized to remit more than 12,200 taels of military service silver owed by Yunnan soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he secured remission of more than 12,200 taels in military service payments owed by Yunnan troops.

sentences.zh: 入覲，以父尹泰老，乞留京侍養。

translations.literal: On entering the capital for audience, because his father Yin Tai was old he begged to remain in the capital to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court for audience, he asked to remain in the capital to care for his aged father Yin Tai.

sentences.zh: 授刑部尚書，兼管兵部。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of the Ministry of Punishments and concurrently directed the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Punishments and given concurrent charge of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 三年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went into mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 四年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，授川陝總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 郭羅克部番復為亂，尹繼善檄諭番酋執為盜者以獻，事旋定。

translations.literal: The tribes of the Golok region rebelled again; Yin Jishan issued orders to the tribal chiefs to seize and deliver up the robbers, and the affair was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Golok tribes rebelled again; Yin Jishan ordered the chieftains to hand over the raiders, and the disturbance was quickly settled.

sentences.zh: 六年。

translations.literal: In the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 奏陳郭羅克善後諸事，請設土目，打牲予號片，寬積案，撤戍兵，上皆許之。

translations.literal: He memorialized on post-pacification matters in Golok, asking to establish native headmen, grant tally slips for hunting, relax accumulated cases, and withdraw garrison troops; the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: He reported on Golok pacification, proposing native headmen, tally slips for hunting parties, relief from backlogged cases, and withdrawal of garrison troops; the emperor approved every item.

sentences.zh: 七年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 八年，署兩江總督，協理河務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs and assisted in river works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he acted as governor-general of the Two Jiangs while assisting with hydraulic affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「毛城鋪天然壩，高郵三壩，皆宜仍舊。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The natural dam at Maochengpu and the three dams at Gaoyou should all be kept as before."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The natural dam at Maochengpu and the three Gaoyou dams should all be maintained as they are."

sentences.zh: 上諭令斟酌，因時制宜。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him to weigh the matter and adapt measures to the times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to weigh the matter carefully and adapt policy to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 九年，衛入覲，還，上命傳旨開天然壩，且曰：「衛奏河水小，壩宜開。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year Wei entered the capital for audience and, on returning, the emperor ordered an edict transmitted to open the natural dam, saying: "Wei reports that the river water is low and the dam should be opened."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Wei came to court and, on his return, the emperor sent orders to open the natural dam, saying: "Wei reports low water and recommends opening the dam."

sentences.zh: 尹繼善覆奏，略言：「衛不問河身深淺，但問河水大小，非知河者也。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan replied in a memorial, stating in brief: "Wei does not ask about the depth of the river channel but only about the volume of the water; he does not understand rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan replied that Wei judged the river only by surface flow, not by channel depth, and therefore did not understand river management.

sentences.zh: 河淺壩開，宣流太過。

translations.literal: When the river is shallow and the dam is opened, discharge becomes excessive.
translations.idiomatic: If the channel is shallow and the dam is opened, the current will be released too forcefully.

sentences.zh: 湖弱不敵黃強，為害滋甚。」

translations.literal: The lake's weak current cannot withstand the Yellow River's strong flow, and the harm will be all the greater."
translations.idiomatic: The lake's weaker current cannot resist the Yellow River's force, and the damage would be severe."

sentences.zh: 上卒用尹繼善議。

translations.literal: In the end the emperor adopted Yin Jishan's view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately followed Yin Jishan's advice.

sentences.zh: 十年，實授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he received regular appointment as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was confirmed as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏言：「阜寧、高、寶諸地圩岸分年修治，務令圩外取土，挑濬成溝，量留涵洞，使旱澇有備。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized: "The polder dikes in Funing, Gaoyou, and Baoying should be repaired year by year; earth must be taken from outside the polders and dredged into channels, with sluice openings left as needed, so that drought and flood may both be provided against.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he wrote: "Polder dikes in Funing, Gaoyou, and Baoying should be repaired on a rotating schedule; soil should be taken from outside the dikes and dredged into drainage channels, with sluices left where needed, so the region is prepared for both drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 鳳、潁、泗三屬頻遭水患，河渠次第開濬，而田間圩塍實與為表裡，亦陸續興修。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Fengyang, Yingzhou, and Sizhou have frequently suffered from floods; canals and ditches are being opened and dredged in turn, while the field dikes are truly their complement and are also being repaired in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang, Yingzhou, and Sizhou have suffered repeated flooding; main canals are being dredged in sequence, and the field dikes that work in tandem with them are likewise being repaired step by step.

sentences.zh: 俟有成效，推行遠近。」

translations.literal: When results are achieved, the practice may be extended near and far."
translations.idiomatic: Once these measures prove effective, they can be extended throughout the region."

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「此誠務本之圖，實力為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "This is truly a plan that addresses fundamentals; carry it out with real effort."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "This is a genuinely fundamental plan; put it into practice with full energy."

sentences.zh: 十三年，入覲，調兩廣，未行，授戶部尚書、協辦大學士、軍機處行走，兼正藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered the capital for audience and was transferred to the Two Guangs, but before departing he was appointed minister of the Ministry of Revenue, associate grand secretary, member of the Grand Council, and concurrently commander of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he came to court and was slated for the Two Guangs, but before he could leave he was made Minister of Revenue, associate grand secretary, Grand Council member, and commander of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復出署川陝總督。

translations.literal: Before long he went out again to serve as acting governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he left the capital again to act as governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 嗣以四川別設總督，命專督陝、甘。

translations.literal: Later, when a separate governor-general was established for Sichuan, he was ordered to supervise Shaanxi and Gansu alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan later received its own governor-general, he was left in sole charge of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 大學士傅恆經略金川，師經陝西，上獎尹繼善料理台站、馬匹諸事，調度得宜。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fu Heng directed the Jinchuan campaign, and the army passed through Shaanxi; the emperor praised Yin Jishan for arranging relay stations, horses, and other matters with proper coordination.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Fu Heng campaigned in Jinchuan and the army passed through Shaanxi, the emperor commended Yin Jishan for his well-managed arrangements of relay stations and horses.

sentences.zh: 十四年，命參贊軍務，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was ordered to assist in military affairs and was given the additional title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was assigned to assist in military planning and received the additional title of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，西藏不靖，四川總督策楞統兵入藏，命兼管川陝總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Tibet was unsettled; Sichuan Governor-General Celeng led troops into Tibet, and Yin Jishan was ordered to take concurrent charge of the Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-generalship.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when Tibet grew unstable, Sichuan Governor-General Celeng marched into Tibet and Yin Jishan was ordered to resume concurrent charge of Sichuan and Shaanxi affairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年，復調兩江。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was again transferred to the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred back to the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，尹繼善以上江頻被水，疏請濬宿州睢河、彭家溝，泗州謝家溝，虹縣汴河上游，築宿州符離橋，靈壁新馬橋，砂礓河尾黃甿橋、翟家橋，詔如所請。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the upper river region had frequently suffered floods, Yin Jishan memorialized to dredge the Sui River and Pengjia Ditch at Suzhou, the Xiejia Ditch at Sizhou, and the upper Bian River at Hong County, and to build the Fuli Bridge at Suzhou, the Xinma Bridge at Lingbi, and the Huangmeng and Zhaijia bridges at the mouth of the Shajiang River; an edict approved his requests.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yin Jishan, citing repeated flooding along the upper river, asked to dredge the Sui River and Pengjia Ditch at Suzhou, the Xiejia Ditch at Sizhou, and the upper Bian River at Hong County, and to build bridges at Fuli, Xinma, Huangmeng, and Zhaijia; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 羅田民馬朝柱為亂，檄總兵牧光宗捕治，並親赴天堂寨，獲朝柱家屬、徒黨，得旨嘉獎，召詣京師。

translations.literal: The Luotian commoner Ma Chaozhu rose in rebellion; Yin Jishan ordered Regional Commander Mu Guangzong to capture and punish him, and went in person to Tiantang Stockade, where he seized Chaozhu's family and followers; he received an edict of commendation and was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Luotian rebel Ma Chaozhu rose in arms, Yin Jishan ordered Regional Commander Mu Guangzong to arrest him and personally went to Tiantang Stockade, capturing Chaozhu's family and followers; he was commended by edict and summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復調署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was again transferred to serve as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred back to act as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，開哈密蔡伯什湖屯田，乾隆初，以畀回民。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign military colonies were opened at Caiboshi Lake in Hami; at the beginning of Qianlong they were handed over to Muslim settlers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, military colonies had been opened at Caiboshi Lake near Hami; early in Qianlong they were turned over to Muslim cultivators.

sentences.zh: 貝子玉素富以屢歉收請罷。

translations.literal: The beile Yusufu, because harvests had repeatedly failed, requested that the colonies be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yusufu asked that the colonies be abandoned after repeated crop failures.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善奏言：「從前開渠引水，幾費經營。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan memorialized: "The earlier opening of canals to draw water cost great effort to arrange.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan argued: "The canals dug to bring in water required enormous effort to establish.

sentences.zh: 回民不諳耕作，頻歲歉收。

translations.literal: The Muslim settlers are unskilled in farming and have had poor harvests year after year.
translations.idiomatic: The Muslim settlers are inexperienced farmers and have suffered poor harvests year after year.

sentences.zh: 萬畝屯田，棄之可惜。

translations.literal: Ten thousand mu of colony fields would be a pity to abandon.
translations.idiomatic: It would be wasteful to abandon ten thousand mu of colony land.

sentences.zh: 請選西安兵丁子弟，或招各衛民承種。」

translations.literal: He asked that sons of soldiers from the Xi'an garrison be selected, or that civilians from the various guards be recruited to take up cultivation."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed assigning sons of Xi'an garrison soldiers or recruiting cultivators from the surrounding guard settlements."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 調江南河道總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be director-general of Jiangnan waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of director-general of Jiangnan waterways.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏言：「河水挾沙而行，停滯成灘。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized: "River water carries sand as it flows; where it stagnates, shoals form.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he wrote: "The river carries silt as it flows, and wherever the current slackens shoals build up.

sentences.zh: 有灘則水射對岸，即成險工。

translations.literal: When shoals form, the water strikes the opposite bank and a dangerous work site is created.
translations.idiomatic: Once shoals appear, the current strikes the opposite bank and creates a dangerous breach point.

sentences.zh: 銅、沛、邳、睢、宿、虹諸地河道多灘，宜遵聖祖諭，於曲處取直，開引河，導溜歸中央，藉水刷沙。

translations.literal: In Tongshan, Pei, Pi, Sui, Su, and Hong the river channels have many shoals; following the Sage Ancestor's instruction, bends should be cut straight, diversion channels opened, the current guided back to the center, and the water used to scour away sand.
translations.idiomatic: From Tongshan through Pei, Pi, Sui, Su, and Hong the channel is shoal-ridden; following the Kangxi emperor's instruction, bends should be straightened, diversion canals dug, the current brought back to mid-channel, and the flow used to scour away silt.

sentences.zh: 河堤歲令加高，務使穩固，而青黃不接，亦寓賑於工。」

translations.literal: River dikes should be raised higher each year to ensure they are firm, and during the lean season between the old and new grain, relief may also be embodied in public works."
translations.idiomatic: Dikes should be raised annually to keep them secure, and during the lean season before the new harvest, public works can also serve as famine relief."

sentences.zh: 詔如議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that his proposals be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 命署兩江總督，兼江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs and concurrently as governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs with concurrent duty as Jiangsu governor.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，疏請濬洪澤湖入江道，開石羊溝，引東西灣兩壩所減之水，疏芒稻閘達董家溝引河，引金灣閘壩所減之水，加寬廖家溝河口，引璧虎、鳳凰兩橋所減之水，並濬各河道上游，修天妃、青龍、白駒諸閘，從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he memorialized to dredge the Hongze Lake outlet to the Yangzi, open the Shiyang Ditch to draw off water reduced by the eastern and western bay dams, dredge the Mangdao Sluice to reach the Dongjiagou diversion, draw off water reduced by the Jinwan dam, widen the mouth of the Liaojiagou, draw off water reduced by the Bihu and Fenghuang bridges, and dredge the upper reaches of the various channels while repairing the Tianfei, Qinglong, and Baiju sluices; all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he proposed dredging Hongze Lake's outlet to the Yangzi, opening the Shiyang Ditch, clearing channels from the eastern and western bay dams, the Mangdao Sluice, the Jinwan dam, the widened Liaojiagou mouth, and the Bihu and Fenghuang bridges, dredging upstream reaches throughout, and repairing the Tianfei, Qinglong, and Baiju sluices; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 實授兩江總督。

translations.literal: He received regular appointment as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was confirmed as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「沛縣地最卑，昭陽、微山諸湖環之，濟、泗、汶、滕諸水奔注。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized: "Pei County lies lowest in elevation; the Zhaoyang and Weishan lakes surround it, and the waters of the Ji, Si, Wen, and Teng rush in.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he wrote: "Pei County is the lowest ground in the region, ringed by the Zhaoyang and Weishan lakes, with the Ji, Si, Wen, and Teng rivers pouring in upon it.

sentences.zh: 請於荊山橋外增建閘壩，使湖水暢流入運。

translations.literal: He asked that sluices and dams be added beyond Jingshan Bridge so that lake water may flow freely into the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed building additional sluices and dams beyond Jingshan Bridge so lake water could flow freely into the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 又沂水自山東南入駱馬湖，出盧口入運，阻荊山橋出水。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Yi River enters Luoma Lake from southeastern Shandong and exits at Lukou into the canal, but its outflow is blocked at Jingshan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi River also enters Luoma Lake from southeastern Shandong and leaves through Lukou for the canal, but Jingshan Bridge blocks its discharge.

sentences.zh: 當相度堵修。」

translations.literal: The site should be surveyed and repairs made by blocking and building up."
translations.idiomatic: The site should be surveyed and appropriate blocking and repair work carried out."

sentences.zh: 上以所言中形勢，嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor found what he had said to fit the situation and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged his analysis to be right about the situation and praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 旋與侍郎夢麟等會督疏治淮、揚、徐、海支干各河暨高、寶各工，是冬事竟，議敘。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Vice Minister Meng Lin and others in jointly supervising dredging of the branch and trunk rivers of Huai, Yang, Xu, and Hai, as well as the works at Gao and Bao; that winter the work was completed and merit was assessed.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Vice Minister Meng Lin and others to supervise dredging of the Huai, Yang, Xu, and Hai river systems and related works at Gao and Bao; the projects were finished that winter and rewards were proposed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上命增設布政使，尹繼善請分設江寧、蘇州二佈政使，而移安徽布政使駐安慶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor ordered additional provincial administration commissioners; Yin Jishan requested that two commissioners be established separately at Jiangning and Suzhou, and that the Anhui commissioner be moved to Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the throne ordered new provincial administration commissioners; Yin Jishan proposed separate posts at Jiangning and Suzhou and relocating the Anhui commissioner to Anqing.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上南巡，命為御前大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when the emperor toured the south, he was appointed an imperial attendant minister.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour in the twenty-seventh year, he was named an imperial attendant minister.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授文華殿大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while remaining in his governor-general post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he received appointment as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and kept his governorship.

sentences.zh: 三十年，上南巡，尹繼善年七十，御書榜以賜。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, during the southern tour, Yin Jishan turned seventy and received an imperially inscribed board as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern tour in the thirtieth year, when Yin Jishan reached seventy, the emperor bestowed a plaque written in the imperial hand.

sentences.zh: 召入閣，兼領兵部事，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He was summoned into the Grand Council, concurrently directed Ministry of War affairs, and served as chief tutor in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was called into the Grand Council, took charge of the Ministry of War as well, and served as chief tutor in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he also served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he also held the chancellorship of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，上東巡，命留京治事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when the emperor toured the east, he was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern tour in the thirty-sixth year, he was left in the capital to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 四月，卒，贈太保，發帑五千治喪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he died, was posthumously made Grand Guardian, and five thousand taels from the treasury were issued for funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month, was posthumously made Grand Guardian, and the court issued five thousand taels from the treasury for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 令皇八子永璇奠醊，永璇，尹繼善壻也。

translations.literal: The Eighth Imperial Son Yongxuan was ordered to offer libations; Yongxuan was Yin Jishan's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The Eighth Imperial Son, Yongxuan—Yin Jishan's son-in-law—was ordered to perform the funeral libations.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，諡文端。

translations.literal: He was granted state sacrificial rites and burial honors, with the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him state funeral rites and the posthumous title Wenduan, Cultured and Upright.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善釋褐五年，即任封疆，年才三十餘。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan had held frontier office only five years after entering official service, and was just over thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Only five years after taking office, Yin Jishan was already serving on the frontier, and he was barely past thirty.

sentences.zh: 蒞政明敏，遇糾紛盤錯，紆徐料量，靡不妥貼。

translations.literal: He was perceptive in governing; when affairs were tangled and complex, he weighed them with deliberate calm and never failed to settle them appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-eyed in office, he handled tangled disputes with unhurried judgment and always found a fitting solution.

sentences.zh: 一督雲、貴，三督川、陝，四督兩江。

translations.literal: He governed Yunnan-Guizhou once, Sichuan-Shaanxi three times, and the Two Jiangs four times.
translations.idiomatic: He served once as governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou, three times of Sichuan-Shaanxi, and four times of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 在江南前後三十年，最久，民德之亦最深。

translations.literal: His tenure in Jiangnan totaled nearly thirty years—the longest of all—and the people cherished him most deeply.
translations.idiomatic: His service in Jiangnan spanned nearly thirty years, longer than any other post, and the people honored him most deeply of all.

sentences.zh: 世宗最賞李衛、鄂爾泰、田文鏡，嘗諭尹繼善，謂當學此三人。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor most admired Li Wei, Ortai, and Tian Wenjing, and once instructed Yin Jishan that he should learn from these three men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yongzheng most admired Li Wei, Ortai, and Tian Wenjing, and once told Yin Jishan that he ought to learn from all three.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善奏曰：「李衛，臣學其勇，不學其粗。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan replied in a memorial: "From Li Wei I would learn his courage, not his roughness.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan answered: "From Li Wei I would take his courage, not his coarseness.

sentences.zh: 田文鏡，臣學其勤，不學其刻。

translations.literal: From Tian Wenjing I would learn his diligence, not his harshness.
translations.idiomatic: From Tian Wenjing I would take his diligence, not his severity.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰，宜學處多，然臣亦不學其愎。」

translations.literal: There is much to learn from Ortai, yet I would not learn his stubbornness either."
translations.idiomatic: There is much in Ortai worth learning, but I would not take his obstinacy."

sentences.zh: 世宗不以為忤。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor did not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yongzheng was not offended.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗謂：「我朝百餘年來，滿洲科目中惟鄂爾泰與尹繼善為真知學者。」

translations.literal: The Qianlong Emperor once said: "In the more than a hundred years of our dynasty, among Manchus who passed the civil examinations only Ortai and Yin Jishan have been true learned men."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianlong once said: "In the more than a century of our dynasty, among Manchus who rose through the civil examinations, only Ortai and Yin Jishan have been genuine scholars.

sentences.zh: 御製懷舊詩复及之。

translations.literal: The emperor's own nostalgic verses also mention him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's own nostalgic poems mention him as well.

sentences.zh: 子慶桂，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Qinggui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinggui is given a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 劉於義，字喻旃，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuyi, styled Yuzhan, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuyi, styled Yuzhan, came from Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi, he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi, Having passed the jinshi examination, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 在翰林文譽甚著，凡有撰擬，輒稱旨。

translations.literal: In the Hanlin his literary reputation was outstanding; whenever he drafted anything it invariably pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His literary reputation in the Hanlin was outstanding, and every draft he produced won imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命直南書房，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was ordered to serve in the Southern Library and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng he was assigned to the Southern Library and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍講，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to reader-in-waiting and appointed educational commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to reader-in-waiting and made educational commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷庶子，上諭以留心民事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made vice supervisor of the Heir Apparent's study, and the emperor instructed him to pay heed to the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became vice supervisor of the Heir Apparent's study, and the emperor told him to keep the people's welfare in mind.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，無積貯，奏請歲以耗羨四萬於太原、平陽、潞安、大同買米貯倉，春糶秋補，上命巡撫伊都立酌量舉行。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, with no stores on hand, he memorialized that forty thousand taels of surplus fees each year should be used to buy grain at Taiyuan, Pingyang, Lu'an, and Datong for storage in granaries, selling in spring and replenishing in autumn; the emperor ordered Governor Neyijili to implement it as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck and there were no reserves, he proposed using forty thousand taels of annual surplus fees to buy grain for granaries at Taiyuan, Pingyang, Lu'an, and Datong, selling in spring and restocking in autumn; the emperor ordered Governor Neyijili to carry this out as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 四年，一歲四遷，擢倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with four promotions in a single year, he was elevated to vice minister of the Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted four times within one year and rose to vice minister of the Granary.

sentences.zh: 倉吏積習，鬻正米以購篩颺耗米抵額。

translations.literal: Granary clerks had a longstanding practice of selling standard grain to purchase screened spoilage grain to meet quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Granary clerks had long sold good grain to buy winnowed spoilage grain so they could meet their quotas.

sentences.zh: 於義嚴出入，稽餘米定數，宿弊一清。

translations.literal: Yu Yi strictly controlled receipts and disbursements, checked surplus grain against fixed amounts, and the entrenched abuses were entirely cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi tightened control over receipts and disbursements, audited surplus grain against fixed quotas, and wiped out the old abuses entirely.

sentences.zh: 七年，命察覈西寧軍需。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to audit military supplies at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was sent to audit military supplies at Xining.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 命與侍郎牧可登如山東察賑，並按按察史唐綏祖劾濟南知府金允彝袒鄒平知縣袁舜裔虧空，論如律。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Shandong with Vice Minister Mu Kedeng to inspect famine relief, and also investigated Surveillance Commissioner Tang Suizu's impeachment of Jinan Prefect Jin Yunyi for shielding Zouping Magistrate Yuan Shunyin in a deficit case; judgment was passed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Shandong with Vice Minister Mu Kedeng to inspect famine relief, and also investigated Surveillance Commissioner Tang Suizu's charge that Jinan Prefect Jin Yunyi had shielded Zouping Magistrate Yuan Shunyin in a treasury deficit; the offenders were sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 九年，授直隸河道總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed canal governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed canal governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 奏天津截留漕糧，省津貼諸費，但給地方官耗米百之一。

translations.literal: He memorialized that grain transport retained at Tianjin should eliminate various subsidy fees, giving local officials only one percent as handling loss.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that grain held at Tianjin should no longer require the various transport subsidies, with local officials receiving only one percent as handling loss.

sentences.zh: 又奏青龍灣諸地，侍郎何國宗議建雞心閘十四阻水，當停。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that at Qinglong Bay and related sites, Vice Minister He Guozong's proposal to build fourteen heart-shaped sluices would obstruct the water and should be halted.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that at Qinglong Bay and nearby areas, the fourteen heart-shaped sluices proposed by Vice Minister He Guozong would block the flow and ought to be stopped.

sentences.zh: 並請展壩面，使無礙水道。

translations.literal: He also asked to widen the dike surface so as not to impede the waterway.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the dike surface be widened so the waterway would not be obstructed.

sentences.zh: 均如議行。

translations.literal: All were approved and carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部尚書，仍理河務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Board of Punishments while continuing to manage river affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of the Board of Punishments while continuing to oversee river works.

sentences.zh: 尋署直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 直隸盜犯，依律不分首從皆斬。

translations.literal: In Zhili, robbers were by law executed without distinction between ringleaders and followers.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhili the law required that robbers be executed without distinguishing ringleaders from followers.

sentences.zh: 大名劫盜十餘案，每案數十人。

translations.literal: In more than ten robbery cases at Daming, each case involved dozens of people.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten robbery cases at Daming had involved dozens of people in each.

sentences.zh: 於義以凶器祗田具，贓物僅米穀，乃饑民借糧爭奪，非盜，奏請得末減。

translations.literal: Yu Yi held that the weapons were only farm tools, the loot merely grain, and that the affair was a scramble among starving people over borrowed grain rather than robbery; he memorialized for reduced sentences at the lower end of the scale.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi argued that the weapons were only farm implements, the goods taken were nothing but grain, and the affair was a fight among starving people over borrowed food rather than robbery; he memorialized for leniency at the lower end of the statutory range.

sentences.zh: 直隸盜案視各省分首從自此始。

translations.literal: From this point Zhili robbery cases, like those of other provinces, began to distinguish ringleaders from followers.
translations.idiomatic: From this case onward Zhili began, like other provinces, to distinguish ringleaders from accomplices in robbery cases.

sentences.zh: 十年，署陝西總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授吏部尚書，仍署總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed minister of the Board of Civil Appointments while still serving as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made minister of the Board of Civil Appointments while continuing as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 累疏言甘、涼為軍需總匯，糧草價昂，兵餉不敷養贍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that Ganzhou and Liangzhou were the main depot for military supplies, that grain and fodder prices were high, and that troop pay was insufficient for their upkeep.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported that Ganzhou and Liangzhou were the chief depot for military supplies, that grain and fodder prices were high, and that soldiers' pay no longer covered their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 請酌借耔糧農器，於瓜州諸地開墾屯種，耕犁以馬代牛，並募耕夫二百，教回民農事。

translations.literal: He asked to lend seed grain and farm tools as appropriate, open fields for colony farming at Guazhou and elsewhere, use horses instead of oxen for plowing, and recruit two hundred farm laborers to teach the Hui people agricultural work.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed lending seed grain and farm tools as needed, opening colony farms around Guazhou, plowing with horses instead of oxen, and hiring two hundred laborers to teach the Hui people farming.

sentences.zh: 又於赤金、靖逆之北湃帶湖及塔兒灣築台堡為保障，安家窩鋪口別開渠供灌溉。

translations.literal: He also built fort platforms at Beipai Dai Lake and Ta'er Bay north of Chijin and Jingni as safeguards, and opened a separate canal at Anjiawopu mouth for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: He also built fortified platforms at Beipai Dai Lake and Ta'er Bay north of Chijin and Jingni for protection, and opened a separate canal at Anjiawopu for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 又疏請甘、涼設馬廠，牧長、牧副，視太僕寺條例，歲十一月，察馬匹孳生多寡，為弁兵升降賞罰。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to establish horse pastures in Ganzhou and Liangzhou with pasture chiefs and deputies, following the regulations of the Court of the Imperial Stud; each November horse breeding numbers would be inspected to determine promotions, demotions, rewards, and punishments for officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to establish horse pastures in Ganzhou and Liangzhou with pasture chiefs and deputies under Court of the Imperial Stud rules, inspecting breeding numbers each November to determine promotions, demotions, rewards, and punishments for officers and men.

sentences.zh: 均如所請行。

translations.literal: All were approved and carried out as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All of these requests were approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命大學士查郎阿代於義領陝西總督，予於義欽差大臣關防，留肅州專筦軍儲。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Grand Secretary Zhalang'a was ordered to replace Yu Yi in heading the Shaanxi governor-generalship; Yu Yi was given the seal of an imperial commissioner and remained at Suzhou in Gansu to manage military stores exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Grand Secretary Zhalang'a was ordered to take over the Shaanxi governorship from Yu Yi; Yu Yi received an imperial commissioner's seal and remained at Suzhou in Gansu to manage military supplies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，奏言：「蘭州浮橋始於前明，用二十四艘，兩埠鐵纜百二十丈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he memorialized: "The Lanzhou pontoon bridge dates from the former Ming dynasty, using twenty-four boats with iron cables of one hundred and twenty zhang between the two banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he reported: "The Lanzhou pontoon bridge dates from the Ming dynasty and originally used twenty-four boats with iron cables one hundred and twenty zhang long between the two banks.

sentences.zh: 自有司遞減四舟，纜僅七十丈，於是埠基砌入河心，水益湍急，衝潰屢見。

translations.literal: Successive local officials reduced it by four boats, leaving cables of only seventy zhang; the bank foundations were thus built into the river channel, the water grew swifter, and breaches were frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials had successively removed four boats, leaving cables of only seventy zhang; the bank foundations were driven into the river channel, the current grew swifter, and breaches became frequent.

sentences.zh: 請動用公帑改復原式。

translations.literal: He requested that public funds be used to restore the original design.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that public funds be used to restore the original design.

sentences.zh: 庶河寬水緩，以便行旅。」

translations.literal: Thus the river would be wider and the water slower, to the convenience of travelers."
translations.idiomatic: That would widen the river, slow the current, and make travel easier."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 查郎阿入覲，於義仍署陝西總督。

translations.literal: When Zhalang'a went to court for an audience, Yu Yi again served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhalang'a went to court for an audience, Yu Yi again served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二年，召還京。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，查郎阿劾承辦軍需道沈青崖等私運侵帑，辭連於義。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhalang'a impeached Grain Transport Commissioner Shen Qingya and others for privately shipping goods and embezzling funds, implicating Yu Yi in the charges.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhalang'a impeached Grain Transport Commissioner Shen Qingya and others for private transport and embezzlement, implicating Yu Yi in the case.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎馬爾泰會查郎阿按治，於義坐奪官，並責償麥稞價銀三萬餘兩。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Malitai to join Zhalang'a in investigating; Yu Yi was stripped of office and ordered to repay more than thirty thousand taels of silver as the value of embezzled wheat grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Malitai to join Zhalang'a in the investigation; Yu Yi was dismissed from office and ordered to repay more than thirty thousand taels of silver for misappropriated wheat grain.

sentences.zh: 甘肅自康熙末至雍正初，虧帑金一百六十餘萬，文書散缺。

translations.literal: From the late Kangxi period to the early Yongzheng period, Gansu had a treasury deficit of more than 1.6 million taels of silver, and its documents were scattered and incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Kangxi reign into early Yongzheng, Gansu had run up a treasury deficit of more than 1.6 million taels, and its records were scattered and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 於義奉命察覈，逮任總督，部署西師往返，凡四年，屯田築堡，安集流移，輸送軍糧戰馬，其勞最多。

translations.literal: Yu Yi was ordered to audit this; once he became governor-general he spent four years organizing the western army's coming and going, establishing colony farms, building forts, resettling displaced people, and supplying military grain and horses—bearing the heaviest burdens of all.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi was ordered to investigate the accounts; once he became governor-general he spent four years organizing the western army's movements, establishing colony farms, building forts, resettling refugees, and supplying grain and horses—bearing more of the burden than anyone.

sentences.zh: 以簿領過繁，得過亦由此。

translations.literal: Because the paperwork was excessively burdensome, his fault arose from this as well.
translations.idiomatic: The sheer volume of paperwork was also how he came to be faulted.

sentences.zh: 五年，起署直隸布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was reinstated and served as acting provincial administration commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was restored to office and served as acting provincial administration commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 七年，授福建巡撫，疏請裁減閩鹽課外加派。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Fujian and memorialized to reduce the additional surcharges on Fujian salt taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Fujian and memorialized to cut the extra surcharges on Fujian salt taxes.

sentences.zh: 漳州民陳作謀、台灣民王永興等謀為亂，遣將吏捕治。

translations.literal: When Chen Zuomou of Zhangzhou and Wang Yongxing of Taiwan and others plotted rebellion, he dispatched generals and officials to capture and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zuomou of Zhangzhou, Wang Yongxing of Taiwan, and others plotted rebellion, he sent officers to capture and punish them.

sentences.zh: 八年，調山西，召補戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shanxi and then summoned to fill the post of minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shanxi and then summoned to serve as minister of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，調吏部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to minister of the Board of Civil Appointments and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made minister of the Board of Civil Appointments and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 御史柴潮生請修治直隸水利，命同直隸總督高斌勘察。

translations.literal: When Censor Chai Chaosheng requested repair of Zhili waterworks, he was ordered to survey the area jointly with Zhili Governor-General Gao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Chai Chaosheng petitioned for repairs to Zhili waterworks, Yu Yi was ordered to inspect the region with Zhili Governor-General Gao Bin.

sentences.zh: 議濬檿牛河；

translations.literal: They proposed dredging the Yan Niu River;
translations.idiomatic: They proposed dredging the Yan Niu River;

sentences.zh: 開白溝河支流，西淀亦開支河，東淀河道裁灣取直，子牙河疏河口，築堤界，別清渾；

translations.literal: opening branch channels of the Baigou River, opening branch rivers in the Western Marsh as well, cutting bends to straighten the Eastern Marsh channel, dredging the mouth of the Ziya River, building dikes to separate clear from muddy water;
translations.idiomatic: opening branch channels of the Baigou River and branch rivers in the Western Marsh, straightening bends in the Eastern Marsh channel, dredging the mouth of the Ziya River, and building dikes to separate clear from muddy water;

sentences.zh: 疏鳳河；

translations.literal: dredging the Feng River;
translations.idiomatic: dredging the Feng River;

sentences.zh: 濬塌河淀；

translations.literal: deepening the Ta River marshes;
translations.idiomatic: deepening the Ta River marshes;

sentences.zh: 引唐河入保定河；

translations.literal: drawing the Tang River into the Baoding River;
translations.idiomatic: diverting the Tang River into the Baoding River;

sentences.zh: 濬正定諸泉，引以溉田；

translations.literal: dredging the springs at Zhengding and channeling them to irrigate fields;
translations.idiomatic: clearing the springs at Zhengding and channeling them for irrigation;

sentences.zh: 並修復營田舊渠閘。

translations.literal: and restoring the old canals and sluices of the colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: and restoring the old colony-field canals and sluices.

sentences.zh: 是為初次應舉各工。

translations.literal: These constituted the first round of proposed projects.
translations.idiomatic: These made up the first round of proposed works.

sentences.zh: 十年，署直隸總督，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting governor-general of Zhili and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting governor-general of Zhili and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是冬，報初次工竟。

translations.literal: That winter came word that the first round of works was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter brought word that the first round of works was finished.

sentences.zh: 复議還鄉河裁灣取直，築運薊河西堤；

translations.literal: They proposed again to cut bends and straighten the Huanxiang River, and to build the western dike of the Yunji Canal;
translations.idiomatic: They proposed again to straighten bends in the Huanxiang River and build the western dike of the Yunji Canal;

sentences.zh: 挑張青口支河、新安新河；

translations.literal: excavating the Zhangqingkou branch river and the Xin'an New River;
translations.idiomatic: excavating the Zhangqingkou branch river and the Xin'an New River;

sentences.zh: 拓廣利渠，望都至安肅開溝；

translations.literal: widening the Guangli Canal and opening a ditch from Wangdu to Ansu;
translations.idiomatic: widening the Guangli Canal and opening a ditch from Wangdu to Ansu;

sentences.zh: 並裁永定河兜灣。

translations.literal: and cutting bends in the Yongding River.
translations.idiomatic: and cutting bends in the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 是為二次應舉各工。

translations.literal: These constituted the second round of proposed projects.
translations.idiomatic: These made up the second round of proposed works.

sentences.zh: 引塌河淀漲水入薊運河；

translations.literal: drawing floodwater from the Ta River marshes into the Ji-Yun Canal;
translations.idiomatic: Channeling floodwater from the Ta River marshes into the Ji-Yun Canal;

sentences.zh: 疏天津賈家口、靜海蘆北口諸河；

translations.literal: dredging the rivers at Tianjin's Jiajiakou, Jinghai's Lubekou, and other sites;
translations.idiomatic: dredging the rivers at Jiajiakou in Tianjin, Lubekou in Jinghai, and other sites;

sentences.zh: 及慶雲馬頰河、鹽山宣惠河。

translations.literal: as well as the Majia River at Qingyun and the Xuanhui River at Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: as well as the Majia River at Qingyun and the Xuanhui River at Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 是為三次應舉各工。

translations.literal: These constituted the third round of proposed projects.
translations.idiomatic: These made up the third round of proposed works.

sentences.zh: 又令署直隸河道總督，疏請減慶雲賦額。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to serve as acting canal governor-general of Zhili and memorialized to reduce the tax quota for Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to serve as acting canal governor-general of Zhili and memorialized to reduce Qingyun's tax quota.

sentences.zh: 上命減地丁十之三，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered land and poll taxes reduced by three-tenths and established this as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered land and poll taxes cut by three-tenths and made the reduction permanent law.

sentences.zh: 十二年夏，報二、三次工竟。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twelfth year came word that the second and third rounds of works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twelfth year came word that the second and third rounds of works were finished.

sentences.zh: 召還。

translations.literal: He was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，奏事養心殿，跪久致僕，遽卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, while presenting memorials in the Hall of Mental Cultivation, prolonged kneeling caused collapse, and he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year, while presenting business in the Hall of Mental Cultivation, he collapsed from kneeling too long and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，諡文恪。

translations.literal: He was granted state sacrificial rites and burial honors, with the posthumous title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him state funeral rites and the posthumous title Wenke, Cultured and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 陳大受，字佔咸，湖南祁陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Dashou, styled Zhanxian, was a native of Qiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dashou, styled Zhanxian, came from Qiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 幼沉敏，初授內則，即退習其儀。

translations.literal: As a child he was sober and quick-witted; when first taught the Inner Canon, he would retire and practice its rites.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was thoughtful and sharp; after his first lessons in the Inner Canon, he would withdraw on his own to rehearse its ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 既長，家貧，躬耕山麓。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, his family was poor, and he personally plowed at the foot of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, his family was poor, and he worked the fields himself at the mountain's foot.

sentences.zh: 同舍漁者夜出捕魚，為候門，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: A roommate who was a fisherman went out at night to catch fish; he kept watch at the door and never stopped reading.
translations.idiomatic: A fisherman who shared his lodging went out at night to fish; Dashou kept watch at the door and never stopped studying.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Yongzheng reign, he passed the jinshi examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, he was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 二年，大考翰詹諸臣，日午，上御座以待。

translations.literal: In the second year, the great examination of Hanlin and Hanlin Academy officials was held; at noon the emperor took the throne and waited.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the Hanlin and Hanlin Academy officials were examined, the emperor took the throne at noon and waited.

sentences.zh: 大受卷先奏，列第一，超擢侍讀。

translations.literal: Dashou's paper was submitted first, ranked first, and he was exceptionally promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou's examination paper was submitted first and placed first; he was exceptionally promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 五遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Within five promotions he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年，授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初視事，決疑獄，老吏駭其精敏。

translations.literal: When he first took office, he decided a doubtful case; veteran clerks were astonished at his acuity.
translations.idiomatic: When he first assumed office, he resolved a doubtful case, and veteran clerks were astonished by his sharp judgment.

sentences.zh: 廬、鳳、潁諸府時多盜，有司多諱匿，大受定限嚴緝，月獲盜五十輩，得旨褒美。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Lu, Feng, and Ying had many bandits at the time; officials often concealed the fact. Dashou set deadlines for strict apprehension; within a month fifty bandits were captured, and he received an imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, Feng, and Ying were then rife with bandits, but local officials often concealed the problem. Dashou set firm deadlines for strict pursuit; within a month fifty bandits were captured, and the emperor praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 淮南、北洊飢，發倉穀賑之。

translations.literal: Huainan and northern Jiangbei suffered repeated famine; he released granary grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan and northern Jiangbei suffered famine year after year; he opened the granaries and distributed grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 穀且盡，繼以麥。

translations.literal: When the grain was nearly exhausted, he continued with wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain was nearly gone, he continued relief with wheat.

sentences.zh: 又告糶江南、廣東，且發且儲。

translations.literal: He also requested sale of grain from Jiangnan and Guangdong, distributing and storing at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested grain sales from Jiangnan and Guangdong, releasing supplies even as he built up reserves.

sentences.zh: 時頻歲饑民掠米麥以食，有司以盜論。

translations.literal: At the time, in consecutive years of famine, starving people plundered rice and wheat to eat; officials prosecuted them as thieves.
translations.idiomatic: In those years of repeated famine, starving people seized rice and wheat to eat, and officials prosecuted them as thieves.

sentences.zh: 哀其情，奏原六十餘人。

translations.literal: Pitying their plight, he memorialized to pardon more than sixty people.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their plight, he memorialized to pardon more than sixty of them.

sentences.zh: 麥熟，禁鵕麴造酒及大商囤積。

translations.literal: When the wheat ripened, he forbade brewing wine from wheat germ and hoarding by large merchants.
translations.idiomatic: When the wheat ripened, he forbade brewing wine from wheat germ and hoarding by large merchants.

sentences.zh: 又以高阜斜陂不宜稻麥。

translations.literal: He also noted that high hills and sloping embankments were unsuitable for rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: He also observed that high ground and sloping embankments were ill suited to rice and wheat.

sentences.zh: 福建安溪有旱稻名畬粟，不須溉灌，前總督郝玉麟得其種，教民試藝有獲。

translations.literal: In Anxi, Fujian, there was a drought-resistant rice called She grain that required no irrigation; former Governor-General Hao Yulin obtained its seed and taught the people to trial-cultivate it with success.
translations.idiomatic: In Anxi, Fujian, there was a drought-resistant rice called she grain that needed no irrigation; the former governor-general Hao Yulin had obtained its seed and taught the people to trial-cultivate it with success.

sentences.zh: 因令有司多購，分給各州縣，俾民因地種植。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered officials to purchase much of it and distribute it to each prefecture and county, enabling the people to plant according to local conditions.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered officials to buy large quantities and distribute the seed to every prefecture and county, so the people could plant according to local conditions.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上諭曰：「諸凡如此留心，甚慰朕懷。」

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor instructed: "In all matters to show such care greatly comforts Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the throne, the emperor said: "To show such care in every matter of this kind greatly comforts my heart."

sentences.zh: 是年，調江蘇，疏請飭糧道較定各州縣漕斛，及先冬令民搜蝻子。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Jiangsu and memorialized requesting the grain-tribute intendant standardize the transport measures of each prefecture and county, and that before winter the people be ordered to search for locust nymphs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Jiangsu and memorialized asking the grain-tribute intendant to standardize transport measures in each prefecture and county, and to order the people to search for locust nymphs before winter.

sentences.zh: 屢諭嘉獎，並以搜蝻子法令直隸總督高斌仿行。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly commended and rewarded him, and ordered the locust-nymph search regulation copied by Governor-General Gao Bin of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly praised and rewarded him, and ordered Governor-General Gao Bin of Zhili to adopt the locust-nymph search regulation as well.

sentences.zh: 常州、鎮江、太倉三府州被水災，發倉治賑。

translations.literal: Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Taicang prefectures suffered flood disasters; he released granary stores for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Taicang were stricken by flood; he opened the granaries and organized relief.

sentences.zh: 江南舊多藉堰圩塘，或有久廢者，被水後尤多潰敗，工鉅費重，民力不能勝。

translations.literal: Jiangnan had long relied on dikes, polders, and ponds, some long abandoned; after the floods many more collapsed; the work was vast and costly, beyond what the people's strength could bear.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had long depended on dikes, polders, and ponds, some of them long neglected; after the floods even more collapsed. The work was enormous and costly, beyond what local people could manage alone.

sentences.zh: 大受出官粟借之，召民興築，計時而成。

translations.literal: Dashou lent out official grain, summoned the people to undertake construction, and the projects were completed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou lent out official grain, mobilized the people to rebuild, and the work was finished on schedule.

sentences.zh: 於江浦繕三合、永豐、北城諸圩，於句容复郭西塘黃堰，蘇州、太倉疏劉家河，灌溉瀦洩，諸工畢舉。

translations.literal: At Jiangpu he repaired the Sanhe, Yongfeng, and Beicheng polders; at Jurong he restored the Huang weir at Guoxitang; at Suzhou and Taicang he dredged the Liujia River—for irrigation, drainage, and storage—and completed all the works.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangpu he repaired the Sanhe, Yongfeng, and Beicheng polders; at Jurong he restored the Huang weir at Guoxitang; at Suzhou and Taicang he dredged the Liujia River. Irrigation, drainage, and flood control were all put in order.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，黃河決古溝、石林，高、寶、興、泰、徐諸州縣罹其患，大受馳視以聞。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, the Yellow River breached at Gugou and Shilin; the prefectures and counties of Gaoyou, Baoying, Xinghua, Taizhou, and Xuzhou suffered; Dashou hurried to inspect and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year the Yellow River broke through at Gugou and Shilin, and Gaoyou, Baoying, Xinghua, Taizhou, and Xuzhou were inundated. Dashou rushed to inspect the damage and report.

sentences.zh: 上命截漕米協濟，大受乃命多具舟，候水至分載四出，舳艫數百里，一日而遍。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered transport grain diverted for mutual relief; Dashou then ordered many boats prepared; when the water arrived they were loaded and dispatched in all directions—a line of vessels stretching hundreds of li, reaching everywhere in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered grain tribute diverted for mutual relief. Dashou had many boats prepared, and when the floodwaters came he loaded them and sent them out in every direction—a line of vessels hundreds of li long, reaching every affected place in a single day.

sentences.zh: 丹陽運河口藉湖水灌輸，淤沙需疏濬，大受奏定六年大修，每年小修。

translations.literal: The Danyang transport canal mouth relied on lake water for irrigation; silt required dredging; Dashou memorialized to fix a major repair every six years and minor repairs annually.
translations.idiomatic: The Danyang transport canal mouth depended on lake water for irrigation and needed dredging as silt accumulated. Dashou memorialized to establish a major repair every six years and minor repairs each year.

sentences.zh: 後高宗南巡，御製反李白丁都護歌曰：「豈無疏濬方，天工在人補。

translations.literal: Later, when the Gaozong emperor toured the south, he composed in response to Li Bai's "Song of Ding the Commandant": "Are there not dredging methods? Heaven's work is supplemented by human effort.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on his southern tour, the Qianlong Emperor wrote a poem in reply to Li Bai's "Song of Ding the Commandant": "Are there not ways to dredge and clear? What heaven leaves undone, human labor must repair.

sentences.zh: 輪年大小修，往來通商賈。」

translations.literal: In rotating years, major and minor repairs—come and go, merchants and traders pass freely."
translations.idiomatic: Major and minor repairs in turn, and merchants and traders pass freely back and forth."

sentences.zh: 蓋嘉其奏定歲修法利於漕運也。

translations.literal: This was to praise his establishment of the annual repair regime that benefited grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote this to praise Dashou's annual repair plan and its benefit to grain transport.

sentences.zh: 十年，有旨蠲明年天下錢糧，大受疏請核准漕項科則，曉諭周知；

translations.literal: In the tenth year, an edict remitted the nation's land tax and grain tribute for the following year; Dashou memorialized requesting verification of transport-tribute tax quotas and broad notification;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year an edict remitted the following year's land tax and grain tribute throughout the empire. Dashou memorialized asking that transport-tribute quotas be verified and the policy made widely known;

sentences.zh: 匯覈地丁耗羨，同漕項並完；

translations.literal: consolidate verification of land tax surcharges and submit them together with transport items as complete;
translations.idiomatic: that land-tax surcharges be consolidated and checked, and submitted together with transport items as complete;

sentences.zh: 酌定業戶減租分數，通飭遵行。

translations.literal: determine the degree of rent reduction for tenant farmers and issue uniform orders for compliance.
translations.idiomatic: and that the degree of rent reduction for tenant farmers be fixed and uniformly enforced.

sentences.zh: 得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: He received an imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 戶部議禁商人貯米，大受謂：「商人貯米，得少利即散，貯不過一歲，民且利焉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated banning merchants from storing grain; Dashou said: "When merchants store grain, as soon as they gain a small profit they sell it; they store for no more than a year, and the people benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue proposed banning merchants from storing grain, Dashou said: "Merchants who store grain sell as soon as they see a small profit; they never hoard for more than a year, and the people benefit.

sentences.zh: 請弛禁便。」

translations.literal: I request that the prohibition be relaxed for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ban be lifted for the public good."

sentences.zh: 又言：「城工核減，意在節用。

translations.literal: He also said: "Reductions in city-wall projects aim at economizing.
