translations.idiomatic: Since the Dzungars had submitted, he also asked that mutual trade markets be established to exchange tea for horses for military use. An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 其治南河，大要因其故道，開通淤淺，俾暢流入海。

translations.literal: In governing the Southern River, his general approach was to follow the old channel, open up silted shallow sections, and allow free flow to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In managing the Southern River section of the Yellow River, his general approach was to follow the old channel, clear silted shallows, and restore unimpeded flow to the sea.

sentences.zh: 督民治溝洫，引水由支達幹，時其蓄洩。

translations.literal: He supervised the people in maintaining ditches and canals, directing water from branch channels to main trunks and regulating storage and discharge in season.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the people in maintaining ditches and canals, channeling water from tributaries into main arteries and regulating storage and release according to the season.

sentences.zh: 徐、海諸州多棄地，遇雨輒淫溢，課民開溝，即以土築圩，多設涵洞為旱潦備；

translations.literal: Xuzhou, Haizhou, and other prefectures had much abandoned land that flooded whenever it rained; he set the people to digging ditches, using the excavated earth to build embankments and installing many culverts as provision against drought and flood;
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou, Haizhou, and neighboring prefectures had much abandoned land that flooded in rain. He set people to digging ditches, using the excavated earth to build embankments and installing culverts as protection against both drought and flood;

sentences.zh: 低地則令種蘆葦，薄其賦。

translations.literal: in low-lying areas he ordered planting reeds and reduced the tax assessment.
translations.idiomatic: in low-lying areas he ordered reeds planted and reduced the tax levies.

sentences.zh: 其在江蘇，尤專意水利，疏丁家溝，展金灣壩，濬徐六涇白茆口，洩太湖水，築崇明土塘禦海潮，開各屬城河。

translations.literal: In Jiangsu he was especially devoted to water control: dredging Dingjia Gully, extending Jinwan Dam, clearing the Xu, Liu, Jing, and Baimao outlets, draining Tai Lake, building earthen seawalls at Chongming against tidal surges, and opening city moats in every jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangsu he devoted himself above all to water management: dredging Dingjia Gully, extending Jinwan Dam, clearing the Xu, Liu, Jing, and Baimao outlets to drain Tai Lake, building earthen seawalls at Chongming against tidal surges, and opening city canals throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「蘇州向設普濟、育嬰、廣仁、錫類諸堂，收養煢獨老病，並及棄嬰。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "Suzhou has long maintained the Puji, Yuying, Guangren, Xilei, and other charity halls, caring for the lonely, infirm, and aged, and also abandoned infants.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Suzhou has long maintained charity halls such as Puji, Yuying, Guangren, and Xilei, caring for the lonely, sick, and aged, as well as abandoned infants.

sentences.zh: 請將通州、崇明濱海淤灘，除附近民業著聽昇科，餘撥入堂。

translations.literal: I request that silt lands along the coast of Tongzhou and Chongming, aside from nearby holdings already under cultivation which may be registered for taxation, be allocated to the charity halls.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that silt lands along the coast of Tongzhou and Chongming, except for nearby parcels already under cultivation which may be registered for taxation, be allocated to the charity halls.

sentences.zh: 又通州、崇明界新漲玉心洲，兩地民互爭，請並撥入，以息爭競。」

translations.literal: Further, the newly risen Yuxin Islet on the Tongzhou-Chongming border is contested by people of both places; I request that it too be allocated to the halls to end the disputes."
translations.idiomatic: The newly risen Yuxin Islet on the Tongzhou-Chongming border is also contested by people on both sides; I ask that it be allocated to the halls as well, to end the strife."

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「不但一舉而數善備，汝亦因此得名也。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "This achieves not only one act but several goods at once—you will also gain renown thereby."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "This achieves several good ends at once—and you will gain renown for it as well."

sentences.zh: 及督湖廣，疏言：「洞庭湖濱居民多築圍墾田，與水爭地，請多掘水口，使私圍盡成廢壤，自不敢再築。」

translations.literal: When governing Huguang, he memorialized: "Residents along Dongting Lake mostly build dikes to reclaim fields, contending with the water for land; I request that many breaches be opened so that private enclosures all become wasteland and people will not dare build again."
translations.idiomatic: While governing Huguang he memorialized: "Residents around Dongting Lake have extensively diked and reclaimed farmland, stealing land from the lake. I ask that many breaches be opened so that private enclosures become wasteland and no one dares build anew."

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「宏謀此舉，不為煦嫗小惠，得封疆之體。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "In this act Hongmou offers no mere small favor of comfort—he grasps the proper stance of a frontier governor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "In this Hongmou is offering no mere petty favor—he understands what a frontier governor ought to be."

sentences.zh: 逮入長吏部，疏言：「文武官弁，均有捕盜之責。

translations.literal: When he entered the capital as head of the Ministry of Personnel, he memorialized: "Civil and military officers alike bear responsibility for apprehending bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered the capital as minister of Personnel, he memorialized: "Civil and military officers alike share responsibility for apprehending bandits.

sentences.zh: 乃州縣捕役，平時豢盜，營兵捕得，就讞時任其狡展，或且為之開脫。

translations.literal: Yet the constables of prefectures and counties habitually harbor thieves; when garrison soldiers make an arrest, at trial they let the culprits cunningly evade charges, or even secure their release.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prefectural and county constables routinely harbor thieves. When garrison soldiers capture a criminal, at trial the constables let him wriggle free through cunning evasions, or even arrange his acquittal.

sentences.zh: 嗣後應令原獲營員會訊。」

translations.literal: Henceforth the original capturing garrison officer should be required to participate in interrogation."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter the garrison officer who made the original arrest should be required to join the interrogation."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其所見切中事理。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his insight as cutting to the heart of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his insight as sound and to the point.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「河工辦料，應令管河各道親驗加結。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "In procuring materials for river works, each river-administration circuit intendant should personally inspect and certify.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "In procuring materials for river works, each river-administration circuit intendant should personally inspect and certify the supplies.

sentences.zh: 失事例應文武分償，而參遊例不及，應酌改畫一。」

translations.literal: In cases of loss, civil and military officers should share liability by precedent, yet vice garrison and patrol commanders are not covered; this should be revised to apply uniformly."
translations.idiomatic: When losses occur, civil and military officers should share liability by precedent, but vice garrison and patrol commanders are not covered. This should be revised so the rule applies uniformly."

sentences.zh: 下河督議行。

translations.literal: The Southern River governor deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern River governor deliberated and carried out the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又言：「匿名揭帖，循例當抵罪，所告款內有無虛實，仍應按治。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Anonymous denunciation postings are by precedent subject to punishment, yet whether the charges within are true or false, they should still be investigated and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: He also stated: "Anonymous denunciation postings are punishable by precedent, but whether the charges they contain are true or false, they should still be investigated and prosecuted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 則宵小不得逞姦，有司亦知所警。」

translations.literal: Thus petty villains cannot practice their schemes, and officials will also know to take warning."
translations.idiomatic: Petty criminals would then be unable to carry out their schemes, and local officials would know to stay on guard."

sentences.zh: 上亦韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor also approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed this as well.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，命協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was ordered to serve as associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，授東閣大學士，兼工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and concurrently minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he became grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and concurrently Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，以病請告，迭諭慰留。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, on grounds of illness he requested leave, but edicts repeatedly urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he asked to retire on account of illness, but the emperor repeatedly urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 三十六年春，病甚，允致仕，加太子太傅，食俸如故。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-sixth year, when his illness was severe, he was permitted to retire, given the additional title Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and allowed to draw his salary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-sixth year, when his illness grew grave, he was allowed to retire with the title Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent while continuing to draw his full salary.

sentences.zh: 賜御用冠服，命其孫刑部主事蘭森侍歸。

translations.literal: He was granted imperial court dress and ordered that his grandson Lanshen, a director in the Ministry of Punishments, attend him home.
translations.idiomatic: The court bestowed imperial robes upon him and ordered his grandson Lanshen, a director in the Ministry of Punishments, to accompany him home.

sentences.zh: 詔所經處有司在二十里內料理護行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered local officials along his route within twenty li to arrange for his escort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed officials along his route to provide escort and provisions within twenty li of each stop.

sentences.zh: 上東巡，覲天津行在，賜詩寵其行。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured the east and he presented himself at the temporary court at Tianjin, the emperor bestowed a poem to honor his journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the east, he presented himself at the temporary court in Tianjin and received an imperial poem honoring his journey.

sentences.zh: 六月，行至兗州韓莊，卒於舟次，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, as he reached Hanzhuang in Yanzhou, he died aboard his boat at the age of seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, while passing Hanzhuang in Yanzhou, he died on board his boat at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 命祀賢良祠，賜祭葬，諡文恭。

translations.literal: He was ordered worshipped in the Temple of Worthies, granted state funeral rites, and given the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was entered in the Temple of Worthies, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 宏謀早歲刻苦自勵，治宋五子之學，宗薛瑄、高攀龍，內行修飭。

translations.literal: In his early years Hongmou disciplined himself rigorously, studied the learning of the Five Masters of the Song, took Xue Xuan and Gao Panlong as his models, and kept his personal conduct in good order.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Hongmou drove himself hard in study, devoted himself to the Five Masters of the Song, took Xue Xuan and Gao Panlong as models, and maintained scrupulous personal conduct.

sentences.zh: 及入仕，本所學以為設施。

translations.literal: Once he entered office, he applied what he had learned in his administration.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he put his learning directly into practice.

sentences.zh: 蒞政必計久遠，規模宏大，措置審詳。

translations.literal: In governing he always planned for the long term, on a grand scale, with careful and thorough arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: In office he always thought in the long term, worked on a large scale, and arranged affairs with careful thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「是非度之於己，毀譽聽之於人，得失安之於數。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Right and wrong are to be measured in oneself; praise and blame are to be left to others; gain and loss are to be entrusted to fate."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Judge right and wrong for yourself, leave praise and blame to others, and accept gain and loss as heaven decrees."

sentences.zh: 輯古今嘉言懿行，為五種遺規，尚名教，厚風俗，親切而詳備。

translations.literal: He compiled fine words and noble deeds from ancient and modern times into the Five Books of Admonitory Precepts, honoring moral teaching, enriching custom, with warmth and thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled exemplary words and deeds from past and present into the Five Books of Admonitory Precepts, upholding moral teaching and enriching local custom in a style at once warm and exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 奏疏文檄，亦多為世所誦。

translations.literal: His memorials, documents, and proclamations were also widely recited in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and official writings were also widely read and quoted in his time.

sentences.zh: 曾孫繼昌，字蓮史。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Jichang, courtesy name Lianshi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Jichang, styled Lianshi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十四年鄉試，二十五年會試、廷試，俱第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, in the provincial examination and in the metropolitan and palace examinations of the twenty-fifth year he ranked first in all, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, he took first place in the provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations of the twenty-fifth year and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷官至江西布政使。

translations.literal: He rose in office to provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：乾隆間論疆吏之賢者，尹繼善與陳宏謀其最也。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Among frontier officials praised as worthy in the Qianlong reign, Yin Jishan and Chen Hongmou were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Of the frontier governors held up as models in the Qianlong reign, none ranked above Yin Jishan and Chen Hongmou.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善寬和敏達，臨事恆若有餘；

translations.literal: Yin Jishan was generous, harmonious, quick, and penetrating, and in handling affairs always seemed to have surplus capacity;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan was open, genial, and quick-witted, and always seemed to have capacity to spare when affairs pressed upon him;

sentences.zh: 宏謀勞心焦思，不遑夙夜，而民感之則同。

translations.literal: Hongmou wore his heart and mind with anxious thought and had no leisure from dawn to dusk, yet the people's gratitude toward them was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmou wore himself out in anxious labor day and night, yet the people cherished both men alike.

sentences.zh: 宏謀學尤醇，所至惓惓民生風俗，古所謂大儒之效也。

translations.literal: Hongmou's learning was especially pure; wherever he went he was earnest about the people's livelihood and local custom—the effect, as the ancients said, of a great Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmou's learning was the purer of the two; everywhere he went he devoted himself to the people's livelihood and local custom—the true effect, as the ancients said, of a great Confucian statesman.

sentences.zh: 於義督軍儲、策水利，皆秩秩有條理。

translations.literal: Yu Yi in supervising military supplies and planning waterworks was in every case orderly and systematic.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, whether supervising military supplies or planning waterworks, was always orderly and systematic.

sentences.zh: 大受剛正，屬吏憚之若神明，然論政重大體，非苟為苛察者比。

translations.literal: Dashou was upright and stern; subordinates feared him as they would a spirit, yet in discussing policy he stressed fundamentals and was not one to indulge in petty scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou was upright and severe; subordinates feared him like a divine judge, yet in policy he stressed fundamentals and was no petty fault-finder.

sentences.zh: 允隨鎮南疆久，澤民之尤大者，航金沙江障洱海，去後民思，與江南之懷尹繼善、陳宏謀略相等，懿哉！

translations.literal: Yunsui long governed the southern frontier; among his greatest benefits to the people were opening navigation on the Jinsha River and controlling the Erhai Lake. After he left, the people missed him, much as Jiangnan remembered Yin Jishan and Chen Hongmou—how admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Yunsui governed the southern frontier for many years; his greatest gifts to the people were opening the Jinsha River to navigation and controlling floods on Erhai Lake. After he left, the people missed him much as Jiangnan missed Yin Jishan and Chen Hongmou—how admirable indeed!
